# 0025: AI-generated assets: PixelLab for pixel art, ElevenLabs for audio, generated by the agent through the owner's connectors and committed with their provenance

- **Status:** Decided; the hero sprite set's cost, checks, hand edits and west still amended 2026-10-19 (Issue-73): skeleton-v3 costs 3 generations a direction for the 6- to 8-frame templates, so a set about 22, as `docs/process/assets.md` now says
- **Date:** 2026-10-18
- **Settles:** where HEAT's art and audio come from, under what licence, how they are made and kept, and the shape of a hero sprite set (Issue-70; the game's look and the sprite pool per class are Issue-71's).

## Decision

**The services.** PixelLab for pixel art and ElevenLabs for sound effects and music. The owner chose them, and holds a subscription to each, because both say they train their models lawfully: ElevenLabs says its music model was trained on licensed data, through deals with Merlin and Kobalt. PixelLab publishes nothing about its training data; that remains a question for PixelLab.

**The licences, on the owner's plans.** HEAT is published by Double Cobra Games LLC, a single-member company, and may later carry ads or take donations.

- PixelLab, Tier 1 (Pixel Apprentice): the creator owns the output and may use it for any purpose, commercial included, except to train other models; the terms do not distinguish plans and give no indemnity. Fits.
- ElevenLabs sound effects, Starter: paid plans may use output commercially, with no attribution. Fits.
- ElevenLabs music, Starter: commercial use is allowed except in film, TV, radio and "Studio Games", and a game under the "Indie Game" revenue line ($500,000 for the game, $1,000,000 a year for the developer) is not a Studio Game, so ads and donations fit. But Starter, Creator and Pro are marked "For Individual Use Only", and whether a single-member company counts is not stated. **No music is made for release until ElevenLabs answers that in writing.** Until then the first plan that plainly fits a company is Scale.
- The owner accepts that generated output may not be protected by copyright, so others could copy it.

**How assets are made.** The agent generates them, through each service's MCP connector attached to the owner's claude.ai account; the token lives only in that connector. Nothing is generated in CI or at build time. ElevenLabs' hosted MCP has no creative tools yet, so audio waits for it.

**How assets are kept.** The generated files are committed under `art/` and are the asset of record. Beside each set, `provenance.json` records what the service's export leaves out: every generation parameter, the service's ids, the plan and the terms' date, the cost. PixelLab's export (version 3.1) holds the frames and the description, size, view and direction count, but not the outline, shading, detail or proportion settings, nor any animation's template or mode.

**A hero sprite set.** `docs/process/assets.md`, rules 8 to 13: a 32 px character on a 48×48 canvas, low top-down, black outline, flat shading, low detail, default proportions, full colour, holding nothing, from one description template; skeleton animations from five PixelLab templates, east only except the walk; about 15 generations a set.

## Considered and not chosen

**Generating at build time or in CI.** The output differs on every call, each call spends the plan's allowance, and CI would need the token.

**A Claude Code entry on the owner's machine** (`claude mcp add` at user scope), the route PixelLab documents. It works and was the first proposal. The owner wanted the connector on the account rather than one machine.

**ElevenLabs' archived local MCP server.** It has the audio tools and needs an API key in a local file, and ElevenLabs no longer maintains it. The hosted one is the supported path.

**ElevenLabs Scale for music now** ($299 a month). It plainly fits a company; it is not bought before ElevenLabs answers the question above.

**A reduced palette.** Each sprite cut to 5 or 6 colours with PixelLab's `reduce_colors`, then all locked to one character's palette; then a master palette of 16 to 24 colours was proposed. In the game's scene at 4× the difference was slight, one character's palette had no colour for blond hair, and the owner preferred full colour.

**Smaller sprites, 16 and 24 px** (Rangers 04 to 07). Closer to Final Fantasy 1's size, and the owner's first aim. At 16 px two sets of one class would differ by a handful of pixels, and PixelLab calls animation below about 20 px unreliable. The owner chose Ranger 01, at 32 px, after seeing all of them in a camp scene.

**Chibi proportions** (Ranger 02, the `chibi` preset) came out brighter and cuter than wanted; **custom proportions** with a bigger head (Ranger 03, head 1.8, arms 0.7, legs 0.6) did not change the figure much; neither was kept.

**Template animations**, at 1 generation a direction against skeleton's 2. The template idle bobbed the head and left stray red pixels; custom-mode animations (a subtle idle, a step-and-raise act, two battle stances) grew 2 to 4 px in height over their loops. Skeleton animations drifted 0 to 2 px and kept the character's colours.

**An idle animation in camp.** The template's head bob looked goofy and a custom idle drifted in size. A standing hero is its still frame, as in NES games.

**A battle stance per role** (melee, agile, caster). It looked right per class but needed per-class art rules; one general stance keeps every class's set the same.

**The cross punch for the act.** Readable, but it says "punch"; the three-frame lead jab is more general, and its reach frame can be held for any action.

**A PixelLab website project to group HEAT's characters.** The MCP's projects are Game Builder projects and the website project is not visible to it; characters are tagged instead.

## Facts checked

All read or measured on 2026-10-18.

- **PixelLab terms of service** (pixellab.ai/termsofservice, last updated 2025-11-23): §3.3 "You retain ownership of any content you create using PixelLab" and outputs may be used "for any purpose"; §1.2, no training of your own models on its images; §2.2, programmatic use only through the official API; §3.3, the user "bear[s] full legal responsibility" for the content; §6.1, no liability for damages.
- **ElevenLabs Terms of Use** (elevenlabs.io/terms-of-use): §1(c), free users "non-commercial purposes", paid users "commercial purposes"; §1(b), use on behalf of an entity; §4(c)(ii), "you retain all rights in and to your Output"; §4(d), ElevenLabs' licence to user content is perpetual and irrevocable.
- **Eleven Music terms** (elevenlabs.io/eleven-music-model-specific-terms, last updated 2026-10-09): Exhibit A, Free to Pro "For Individual Use Only", Scale "Individuals, or entities or organizations with fewer than 10 employees", media rights on every plan below Enterprise Music "except film, TV, radio, and Studio Games"; §4.8(c) and (j), the Indie Game and Studio Game definitions; §4.7, 60 days after a game stops being an Indie Game; §1.5, on upgrade the output in the account takes the upgraded plan, and on downgrade output "remains subject to the plan in effect when that Output was created".
- **ElevenLabs sound effects** (elevenlabs.io/sound-effects/game): "all ElevenLabs Sound Effects are royalty free and can be used in commercial projects"; the free plan requires attribution and paid plans do not.
- **ElevenLabs MCP** (elevenlabs.io/mcp; github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-mcp): the hosted server manages agents, creative tools "coming soon"; the local server is archived.
- **PixelLab MCP** (pixellab.ai/mcp and the connector's own tool descriptions): bearer-token authentication; `create_character` standard mode 1 generation; `palette` and `max_colors` refused outside pro mode; `skeleton-v3` charged 2 generations for one direction at this size, from the receipt.
- **Custom connectors** (claude.com/docs/connectors/custom/add-unlisted): a fixed credential goes in a request header with No sign-in, sent exactly as entered; headers cannot be edited after saving.
